function: Multi-agent DRL learns UAV charging (WPT) time allocation and UAV trajectories for energy efficiency; IRS phases closed-form, UAV association by matching, not learned (p. 5, p. 8).
system: Single-antenna UAVs and devices (scalar channels, p. 4); 10-140 reflecting IRSs with K=20 elements; 3-7 UAVs; band not stated, 1 kHz bandwidth (p. 9).
method: Reinforcement learning: multi-agent actor-critic with value-decomposition mixing network (FACMAC-based), GRU actor, centralized training and decentralized execution, trained offline (p. 5-7, p. 9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician UAV-device channel (factor 10 dB) and LoS UAV-IRS, IRS-device links; UAVs, devices random in 500 m x 500 m (p. 4, p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Perfect CSI (p. 3). Training shown for 20 devices, 7 UAVs; tests over 10-140 devices (4 UAVs), 3-7 UAVs (20 devices); per-setting convergence time (p. 9-12).
baselines: Learned: SCR [41] and MADRL-PPO [42] (DRL); heuristics: time equalization (fixed equal charging/data split) and random association, both multi-agent DRL variants (p. 10, p. 12).
metrics: System energy efficiency (bits/joule), number of uploaded bits, system energy consumption, cumulative training reward, execution time and convergence time (p. 9, p. 11).
complexity: Execution complexity O(EN(U(2FinFout+UinUh+Uh)+MU+MUKI)) (Theorem 2); measured execution and convergence time vs. number of devices (Fig. 7) (p. 8, p. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 4: "Rician channel model [14], denoted as follows"; p. 4: "it is assumed that they both belong to the LoS channel". Custom Rician/LoS simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 9: "By setting the number of IoT devices to 20 and the number of UAVs to 7, we show the change in cumulative rewards"; p. 12: "algorithms need to spend more time to learn a good policy". Devices and UAVs are swept, but no trained model is stated to be tested in an unseen setting; per-setting convergence time suggests retraining.
q3_support: p. 10: "SCR [41]: It is a centralized DRL-based algorithm"; p. 10: "MADRL-PPO [42]: It is a multi-agent DRL-based distributed algorithm"; p. 10 (TE, fixed allocation): "equally divided into charging time and data transmission time"; p. 10: "system energy efficiency of LIBRA algorithm is consistently higher than that of the other four algorithms".
q4_support: p. 8: "The complexity of LIBRA algorithm in the execution phase is O(EN (U (2Fin Fout + Uin Uh + Uh ) + M U + M U KI))"; p. 11: "Performance of execution and convergence time." (Fig. 7, measured runtime).
q5_support: p. 8: "We conduct extensive simulations based on Pytorch 1.8.1 and Python 3.9". Simulated channels only; no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Eligibility: the multi-agent DRL learns UAV trajectories (above PHY) and each UAV's WPT charging-time allocation (p. 5: "we first design a multi-agent DRL-based algorithm to learn UAV trajectories and charging time allocation policies"). IRS phases come from closed-form phase alignment (Theorem 1, p. 8) and UAV association from a matching algorithm (Algorithm 3, p. 8-9), so the RIS configuration is not learned. I read the learned charging/data time split of the UAV-device link as resource allocation of an aerial link (p. 10: "The TE algorithm does not schedule time resources rationally"), physical layer under the aerial-link clause of Step 1 and learned jointly with the trajectories, so above_phy does not apply; area 6, not 3 (6 would also win over 3). Reviewer to confirm this borderline. q3: the non-learned baseline is TE, a fixed equal charging/data split; TE and RA otherwise keep the multi-agent DRL (p. 12: "the other four distributed multi-agent DRL approaches"). Single antennas are implied by the scalar channels, not stated. Table I labels the Rician factor "Rayleigh factor" (10 dB); no carrier frequency is given.
